integration_notes:
This is the demo-programs slice of the request: five stress programs for the defence demos. It is not the boot screen, logo or other UI work. Nothing outside apps/demo/ was edited. Before the programs can run from the Terminal:

1. Program registry and /bin: import DEMO_PROGRAMS (or demoProgram(name)) and DEMO_MANIFESTS from apps/demo/index.ts into whatever loads programs onto executors and seeds /bin/<name>.json. apps/src/index.ts (owned by R3) exports nothing of the demo yet. The manifest `entry` values are placeholders ('apps/demo/<name>'). burn and memhog spawn their children from the hard-coded paths /bin/burn.json and /bin/memhog.json, so those must exist. burn, memhog and lockdemo are checkpointable: true; mktree and idx50k are not.

2. Man pages: copy apps/demo/man/*.md to /usr/share/man/1/ and add them to /usr/share/man/index.json, where coreutils `man` reads pages. After editing a man page's front matter, run `node apps/demo/scripts/gen-argspec.mjs` (`--check` verifies).

3. Sys client: the programs use @plotinium/kernel/sys (ctx.sys stubs, ctx.sleep, ctx.tick), not apps/src/_sys.ts. Argument parsing reuses the generic parser in apps/coreutils/lib/argspec.ts.

4. ctx.mem (R1): kernel/sys ProgramContext has no `mem` yet (it is a TODO there). memhog looks for ctx.mem shaped `{ alloc({kind:'chunk', size, label}) -> SysGen<{pageIds}>, get(id, 'r'|'rw') -> SysGen<Uint8Array|ArrayBuffer>, free(ids) -> SysGen }`, following memory-and-paging.md §4.2 (the type is CtxMem in apps/demo/lib/pages.ts). Until that lands it falls back to one protocol `mem.alloc({bytes, key:'memhog.<child>.<page>', kind:'buffer'})` per 256 KiB page plus `mem.free({segId})`. Every byte is still reserved and accounted, but the page bodies live in the generator frame and are rebuilt from their seeds after a restore. So until ctx.mem exists, page-in is not truly tested byte-for-byte.
   - get() must return the page's live buffer and a written page must count as dirty. get() must also re-fault if the page was evicted again before the process runs; the fake kernel does this.
   - Mismatch to resolve: kernel/src/core/mm/mm.ts alloc takes {kind:'logical'|'chunk'|'segment', size, label} -> {pageIds}, while the protocol's mem.alloc takes {bytes, key?, kind?:'state'|'buffer'} -> {segId}. The syscall handler or the protocol needs to settle this.

5. Protocol requests (R1): add `exclusive?` to SpawnArgs (burn --exclusive passes it and treats EINVAL/EPERM as refused, prints a warning and runs shared). Add `committed`, `oldestBlockedMs` and `maxOverBudgetMs` to MemStat; memhog reads them when present and prints '-' otherwise.

6. Capabilities: idx50k's manifest lists 'ai.search', but that cap is not in the user bounding set (protocol/src/caps.ts). If `ai.semsearch` is checked against 'ai.search', `idx50k --wait` will fail with a permission error until 'ai.search' is added to the user bounding set (rag-semantic-search.md asks for it as a default).

7. Demo defaults:
   - With default arguments, mktree builds exactly tests/fixtures/trees.ts tree1000 (manifest sha256 5c9b2025…f430, 210 directories, 1,609,683 bytes, depth 13), so the server seed and the fault-injection oracle agree with it.
   - idx50k writes 51,200 bytes to ~/idx50k.md.
   - lockdemo assumes the kernel renews the lease heartbeat and releases a process's leases when it exits (PROC-07).
